Everyone working in social care should develop the skills to use care technologies and software as required for their role.

Solve basic problems when using technology

Know what to do if you experience a technical problem. This may include:

following instructions set out in your organisation’s policies and procedures

using the device or software manual to help you solve the problem

using the internet, chat facilities or technical support helplines where available

using online tutorials, FAQs and advice forums

If you are unsure what to do, speak to your manager or supervisor, a digital champion or similar contact in your organisation.

Go further (theme 2)

Support or lead the set up, implementation and ongoing maintenance of technology in your organisation

Support the implementation of new technology, including preparing staff and supporting new ways of working.

You may also need to work with technology suppliers to make sure installation runs smoothly.

Model how to use different types of technology safely, and help others use technology in their day-to-day work

You can support your colleagues by:

promoting the use of technology to support quality care

demonstrating how you use technology in a safe and effective way

offering advice if you notice mistakes or unsafe practices

Support others to solve problems and access learning opportunities to improve their digital skills and confidence

Support colleagues to solve technical problems and access learning opportunities.

You can do this by:

supporting colleagues with troubleshooting and problem-solving, either directly or by helping them access specialist technical support

making sure common problems are learned from across your organisation

Stay up to date with technology and proactively explore new digital tools

Keep up to date with new technologies, championing their benefits and recognising success and innovation. This will help you make sure your service is continuously learning and improving, in line with the well-led part of the Care Quality Commission’s (CQC) assessment framework.

Theme 3: communicating using technology

This theme covers the skills staff need to communicate effectively and safely using technology.

Digital skills for all (theme 3)

Understand the different methods of digital communication and why we use them

Use digital communication tools appropriately in your role. Examples include:

email

messaging platforms

sending messages through specialist apps or DSCR systems

online forums

video and phone calls

You should always communicate information safely and securely, especially when sharing information about people. For further guidance see theme 4: using and managing data.

Choose the right type of communication technology for the situation and adapt your communication style as necessary

You should understand the digital communication tools available, and which tools are right for a particular situation or the needs of the person you are communicating with.

Use communication technologies safely

All staff should be able to use communication technologies safely and appropriately. This may include supporting others to use communication technologies. Use digital communication respectfully and in line with your organisation’s policies, including any policies on the use of social media.

Work with others using digital tools

Contribute to shared digital workspaces and documents when working with others.

There are also many online forums where social care staff can share news, tips and advice. Your local care association may be able to recommend relevant groups and forums.

Support others to use digital communication tools to stay connected

You should be able to help others use a range of technologies that can help them to keep in touch with family, friends and their community.

Go further (theme 3)

Lead in modelling and promoting good practice in digital communication

You can support your colleagues to develop their digital communication skills by modelling and promoting appropriate use of communication technology in the workplace. You can also highlight the benefits of online forums for learning and collaboration.

Help colleagues use communication technologies safely and choose the right tool for the situation

Use a range of resources to help your colleagues communicate safely using technology.

Contribute to developing policies and procedures for safe and appropriate digital communication in your organisation

Develop and maintain policies and procedures for safe, accessible digital communication. As digital communication becomes more widely used in the provision of care, staff in leadership and management roles should make sure appropriate policies and procedures are in place to support good practice.

Care providers are also required to make sure communication happens safely, with appropriate data security arrangements in place. For further guidance see theme 5: being safe and secure online.

Theme 4: using and managing data

This theme covers the skills staff need to use, share and manage data safely.

Digital skills for all (theme 4)

Understand the different types of data and know how data can be collected, kept up to date and shared using technology

Data about someone you’re supporting can be stored and shared digitally in different ways. For example, by entering information into an app or sharing it by text or email. Information relating to someone’s care may be classified as personal data, special category data or confidential data. There are different rules for handling these types of information.

For more guidance, see data security awareness courses on the e-learning for healthcare website.

Understand your personal responsibilities for managing data

Use technology to monitor your own development and, where applicable, the development of those you manage or supervise

Use technology to monitor and record learning and development activities for yourself and those you manage or supervise. Use this information to make sure staff are up to date with mandatory training requirements and provide evidence of training to regulators and other organisations.

Create opportunities for staff to learn from each other

Explore opportunities to learn from other organisations through digital forums and online communities, to share best practice and support business development.

Support colleagues to manage their digital wellbeing

Promote a culture of respectful digital interaction in your organisation and take action if you become aware of inappropriate practices.

Make sure staff are fully supported to manage their digital wellbeing. This includes promoting open, non-judgemental conversations about technology and digital learning, and offering support and reassurance to those who feel anxious using technology.

In line with CQC’s assessment framework, you should actively seek out and promote digital wellbeing support within your organisation to help look after staff health and wellbeing.
